match.reason: None of the bank points covers graph theory: they all teach function graphs (logarithms, dilations, solving equations, rules from graphs, cubics), not simple, complete, bipartite or regular graphs, subgraphs, complements or isomorphism.

draft.title: Types of graphs
card: a graph with no loops and no more than one edge between any two vertices. Every graph here is simple.
every pair of vertices is joined by an edge. Kn has n vertices and n(n − 1)/2 edges. K5 has 5 × 4 ÷ 2 = 10 edges.
every vertex has the same degree. A regular graph with degree 3 is called 3-regular.
the complement of a simple graph has the same vertices and exactly the edges the graph lacks. A graph and its complement together make a complete graph.
draft.remember: A complete graph has every possible edge. The complement has exactly the edges that are missing.

a.q: A simple graph has 6 vertices and is complete. How many edges does it have?
a.why: K6 has 6 × 5 ÷ 2 = 15 edges. Choosing 6 × 5 = 30 forgets that each edge is counted twice, once from each end.
a.clue: Count each edge once, not from both ends.

b.q: A simple graph has 5 vertices and 4 edges. What is the number of edges in its complement?
b.why: K5 has 5 × 4 ÷ 2 = 10 edges. The graph and its complement together make K5, so the complement has 10 − 4 = 6 edges. Giving 4 wrongly treats the complement as having the same edges.
b.clue: Find the edges of the complete graph on 5 vertices first.

check.summary: No problems found. Both questions have one correct answer (15 and 6), consistent with the card and the explanations.
